questions.question: Describe the roles of men and women in early farming societies.
questions.expected_answer: Men mostly cared for the cattle, cleared new fields, built the frames of houses and kraals, hunted, defended the community, worked iron and took part in council. Women mostly grew the crops, ground grain, cooked, brewed beer, fetched water and firewood, cared for young children, plastered and smeared houses and made pots and baskets.

questions.question: Explain how children helped their families to produce food.
questions.expected_answer: Boys looked after goats, sheep and calves, and later herded the cattle. Girls helped in the fields and at home, fetched water and firewood, ground grain and cared for younger children. Both boys and girls chased birds from the ripening grain. They learnt skills by working with adults.

questions.question: Explain what initiation was and why it mattered.
questions.expected_answer: Initiation was a set of ceremonies and teachings marking the step from childhood to adulthood, usually around the teenage years. Boys and girls were taught separately by older men and women about customs, duties and respect. Afterwards they were treated as adults and could marry, and boys initiated together often formed a lifelong age group.
